title: C482/1165/2012 of SWAMI CHETAN MUNI SWACHETNA DHAM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No.1165 of 2012
(U/s 482 Cr.P.C.)
Swami Chetan Muni Swachetna Dham
ÖÖÖ..Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another
ÖÖÖRespondents
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Having heard Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Advocate, for the
petitioner and Mr. Navneesh Negi, Brief Holder, for the State, it
appears that the challenge herein is to the order of cognizance
dated 28.02.2009 passed by the First Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar in complaint case no.245 of 2009 State
Vs. Ram Lotan and others, asking the petitioner Chetan Muni
as well as Ram Lotan and Ram Dhan to face trial for the
offences under Section 9, 50, 51 and 52 of the Wild Life
(Protection) Act (hereinafter to be referred as the Act) .
 The incident, in question, relates way back to 18.3.1998
at 10 A.M., when a dead male elephant was found within the
precincts of village Haripur Kalan, District Haridwar. The
elephant purportedly died because of electrocution, on
account of touching the current flowing wire, meant to protect
some agricultural produce in and around the ëAshramí. When
the forest officials reached at the spot, the main culprit Chetan
Muni (petitioner) absconded from the spot, whereas his
servitors Ram Lotan and Ram Dhan were arrested, who too
were released subsequently on presentation of personal bonds.
 On 16.12.1999, the complaint, in question, was filed
after making the necessary enquiry, as envisaged under the

2
Act but it appears that a petition no.418 of 2001 u/s 482
Cr.P.C., was filed challenging the order of cognizance passed
by the Magistrate on the said complaint. The said petition was
adjudicated by this Court on 4.12.2008, whereby the
cognizance order was set aside and the matter was remanded
to the concerned Magistrate to proceed with the case afresh
after going through the entire record of the case. The
observation made by this Court was that the Magistrate
passed the summoning order in a mechanical manner without
any application of mind regarding the evidence available on
record.
 Thereafter the matter again came up before the
Magistrate concerned, who passed the order of cognizance
afresh on 28.2.2009, which has once again been challenged by
way of instant petition before this Court.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner has vociferously
argued that the statements of co-accused Ram Lotan and Ram
Dhan ought not to have been made basis for filing the
impugned complaint. This contention is not acceptable and is
rejected out rightly for the reason that the order of cognizance
is reasoned not solely upon the basis of statements of those
two co-accused, but also on the basis of other overwhelming
evidence which has been narrated in the later portion of the
complaint.
 Apart from above, the statements of Ram Lotan and Ram
Dhan can very well be taken into consideration being the
accomplice and the same thus, cannot be discarded in order to
arrive at truth. The Court feels that the sole motto of main
culprit Chetan Muni, who is the petitioner before this Court, is
to prolong and hamper the trial against him, which has
already been delayed for more than a decade. All the more,
the court below has filed the instant petition, expressing its

3
elaborate reasons before summoning the accused. The Court
feels that it is an abuse of process of law and also of Court on
the part of present petitioner.
 Therefore, in view of what has been stated above, the
Court hereby dismisses the petition in limine but at the same
time, imposes costs of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand
only) against the petitioner for his mischievous attempt to defy
and delay every procedure of law. Let a copy of this order be
sent by fax to the court concerned, which shall take the
coercive measures to ensure the presence of petitioner as well
as about the recovery of costs, so imposed by this Court. The
costs, so deposited, shall subsequently be deposited in the
government treasury.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
08.11.2012
Rdang
